questions.stem: Why do ionic compounds have high melting points?

options.text: Because they contain delocalised electrons
Because there are strong electrostatic forces between the ions in all directions
Because the molecules are very large
Because they contain strong covalent bonds

questions.explanation: Ionic compounds have high melting points because a large amount of energy is needed to overcome the strong electrostatic forces of attraction between the oppositely charged ions in the giant lattice.

questions.stem: When can an ionic compound conduct electricity?

options.text: Never, ionic compounds cannot conduct electricity
Only when solid
When molten or dissolved in water, but not when solid
Under all conditions

questions.explanation: Ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water because the ions are free to move and carry charge. When solid, the ions are held in fixed positions and cannot move.

questions.stem: What is the formula of magnesium chloride?

options.text: MgCl
Mg₂Cl
MgCl₂
Mg₂Cl₂

questions.explanation: Magnesium forms Mg²⁺ ions and chlorine forms Cl⁻ ions. Two Cl⁻ ions are needed to balance the 2+ charge on Mg²⁺, giving the formula MgCl₂.

questions.stem: Why are ionic compounds often soluble in water?

options.text: Because water is a strong acid
Because ionic compounds are always liquids
Because water molecules can break the ions apart from the lattice
Because ionic compounds have weak bonds

questions.explanation: Water molecules are polar and can surround the individual ions, pulling them away from the lattice and dissolving the compound. The ions become hydrated.

questions.stem: What is the overall charge of an ionic compound such as NaCl?

options.text: Positive
Neutral (zero)
It varies
Negative

questions.explanation: Ionic compounds are always electrically neutral overall. The total positive charges from the cations balance exactly with the total negative charges from the anions.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the structure of sodium chloride?

options.text: A regular three-dimensional lattice of alternating Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions
A random arrangement of sodium and chlorine atoms
Layers of sodium atoms with chlorine atoms in between
Pairs of Na and Cl atoms bonded together as molecules

questions.explanation: Sodium chloride forms a giant ionic lattice where Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions alternate in a regular three-dimensional pattern. Each ion is surrounded by ions of the opposite charge.

options.text: Because applying force shifts layers so like-charged ions align, causing repulsion and shattering
Because they contain delocalised electrons
Because they have weak bonds between ions
Because they are made of non-metals

questions.explanation: When a force displaces the layers in an ionic lattice, ions of the same charge can line up next to each other. The strong repulsion between like charges causes the lattice to shatter.
